audit_2026_10_18: AUDIT GATE PASSED (first-hand, 2026-10-18) — unlike Harris (session 11) and Dallas (session 12), Fort Worth publishes a current, official, bulk-accessible permit record. CHANNELS CHECKED: (1) The legacy Socrata portal data.fortworthtexas.gov is GONE — the domain now fronts an ArcGIS Hub site and the SODA endpoint 302-redirects to hub.arcgis.com/legacy; the Socrata catalog still carries a stale index entry (quz7-xnsy 'Development Permits', monthly-updated Accela extract, created 2014) but the live catalog is the Hub. (2) ArcGIS Hub (org 3ddLCBXe1bRt7mzj, publisher City of Fort Worth, owner CFW_AGOL_ADMIN): 'CFW Development Permits Table' (hosted FeatureServer view, services5.arcgis.com) + 'CFW Development Permits Points' (the same Accela mirror with geometry, mapit.fortworthtexas.gov) are the org's only record-level permit services (full owner sweep: 13 permit-titled items — maps/apps referencing these two services, plus gas-well pads). Item description: 'all permits issued through the Development Services permit center: building, mechanical plumbing, garage sales and others. Data is updated hourly during business hours.' License: CC BY 4.0 (item licenseInfo); access public; accessInformation 'City of Fort Worth Development Services Department'. (3) Tarrant County side: no county building-permits product exists (ArcGIS sweep finds only a county utility-permit map service and oil-well viewers; no Socrata catalog hits) — the Cook/King city-feed route with honest labeling is the only route, and here the city feed exists. MEASURED CADENCE (not the description's claim): layer editingInfo.dataLastEditDate 2026-10-16T21:25:29Z (a Friday evening UTC) and the newest File_Date in the data is 2026-10-16 — hourly business-hours updates with a normal weekend pause; gate 5 measures the layer stamp under a 96h threshold. THE RECORD: 1,619,480 rows all-time (File_Date 2001-06-30 onward), the city's Accela permit-center mirror (B1_* fields). It is an ALL-APPLICATIONS register, not an issued-only register (contrast San Antonio): Current_Status spans the full workflow (Finaled 1,284,701 / Expired 200,227 / Issued 46,665 / Void / Withdrawn / Pending / Plan Review / Approved / Denied ...). It publishes exactly two dates — File_Date (application filed) and Status_Date (when the CURRENT status was reached; for Finaled rows that is the final-inspection date, measured 21-34 days after filing on samples) — and NO issuance date. Published population is therefore defined by status (see dedupe_rule/scope), never by a status date. Trailing-12-months volume measured from the source itself: 75,570 rows filed (File_Date >= 2025-10-18); 70,020 in the issued-proven status set (>= 2025-10-18) / 70,199 (>= 2025-10-17); scoped published pull 70,006 rows (see scope filter).
coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of Fort Worth (Development Services Department) only. Other Tarrant County jurisdictions (Arlington, and the county's unincorporated-area permitting) publish their permits separately and are not in this feed; totals here are City of Fort Worth totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one Permit_No in the City of Fort Worth's Development Permits table, counted when the permit stands in a status that can only be reached after issuance (registry pull_where_extra scope). The feed's grain is MOSTLY one row per permit, with a measured fan-out: surplus rows are the same permit restated — per address it covers (the San Francisco shape) and per-record duplicates of the mirror extract (the extreme case is one Finaled electrical permit, PE26-01700, restated on 1,024 rows identical on every substantive field). The pipeline collapses each permit's rows into one record (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the representative row is the permit's earliest-filed row (pull order: File_Date, Permit_No, ObjectId). Monthly counts are by the permit's File_Date month — the city dates applications, not issuances (see field_map.issue_date).
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (File_Date >= '2025-10-17'), issued-proven status set, measured 2026-10-18 on a full audit pull verified against source-side counts (70,199 rows both ways): 70,199 rows = 63,948 distinct Permit_No (61,981 permits x 1 row; 1,967 permits fan out to 2-1,024 rows; surplus 6,251 rows). Across all 1,967 multi-row groups the rows NEVER disagree on Permit_Type, Permit_SubType, or JobValue (0 groups each, NULL-sensitive) — the collapse asserts exactly those three fields and the production run must report field_disagreements {}. Rows inside a group DO vary on address parts (440 groups), current status within the issued-proven set (148), status date (151), and file date (25) — the representative-row rule above governs those fields, and it is printed on the county hub.

field_map.address: Composed from the address parts the table publishes (Addr_No + Direction + Street_Name + Street_Suffix + Street_Suffix_Dir); the table's own Full_Street_Address column is unpopulated on sampled rows, so the parts are the record. ZIP from Zip_Code (integer).
field_map.application_date: File_Date — the date the application was filed with the city (the dataset column's own description).
field_map.category: Derived from Permit_Type's own Residential/Commercial naming for the building and accessory families only (Residential Building Permit, Residential Accessory Struct -> residential; Commercial Building Permit, Commercial Accessory Structure, Commercial Grading Permit -> commercial); the trade families publish no class and stay NULL (honest NULL). The feed's Permit_Category column is 'NA' on 1,532,076 of 1,619,480 rows and is not used.
field_map.contractor_rule: NONE CARRIED — the table publishes no contractor or business field at all. Its only name field is Owner_Full_Name (property-owner person names); it is excluded from the pull's column list entirely and never requested. B1_SPECIAL_TEXT ('additional information about who was involved in the permit') is likewise never requested. contractor_name stays NULL, never inferred (the Boston treatment).
field_map.issue_date: File_Date, LABELED AS SUCH. The feed publishes no issuance date: its only other date, Status_Date, is when the record's current status was reached (for Finaled permits, the final-inspection date — not issuance). Published counts are therefore permits that have been issued (status evidence), counted in the month the application was filed; recent months grow as filed applications complete review and reach an issued status. This definition is printed on the county hub, the Data Sources page, and llms.txt.
field_map.permit_number: Permit_No (Accela record number; PB/PP/PE/PM-prefixed by family and year).
field_map.status: Current_Status, restricted at pull time to the issued-proven set (see scope) and mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source.
field_map.valuation: JobValue (a TEXT column; parsed to float, unparseable -> NULL). The value belongs to the permit, not the row: a permit's rows never disagree on it (measured, 0 of 1,967 multi-row groups), so the permit's value is its rows' single stated figure, counted ONCE (the NYC restatement shape, neutralized by the collapse). COVERAGE IS BINARY BY FAMILY (measured at permit level on the full window pull): the building families state a value on ~100% of permits (Residential Building 10,873/10,873; Commercial Building 1,384/1,388; Residential Accessory 1,301/1,381; Commercial Accessory 818/818) and the trade families state one on 0% (Plumbing 0/15,594; Electrical 0/14,219; Mechanical 0/11,680; Backflow 0/7,624) — the city collects job value on building permits and not on trade permits, so the valued population IS the money population. Permit level: 14,376 of 63,948 permits state a figure (22.5%), only 81 at $0/$1 combined (0.1% — the Austin placeholder disease is absent), median positive $125,000, all values parseable. VALUES PUBLISH as reported under the count-once rule: window total $6,868,935,103.89 on the audit pull (the production DB sum must reproduce the source-side figure for the identical scoped window exactly). Disclosed shapes: one genuine mega-project (a $523,500,000 hospital building permit, 7.6% of the total — the Chicago shape); the JPS medical project states $264,000,000 on each of two phase permits (dark shell; finish-out) — if that figure is the whole project's value restated, worst-case overstatement is $264,000,000 (3.8%), the Baton Rouge bound, printed on Data Sources.

history_range: File_Date 2001-06-30 onward in the source; we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) — the license named in the ArcGIS item record for CFW Development Permits Table; figures attributed to the City of Fort Worth
pull_where_extra: Current_Status IN ('Issued','Finaled','Expired','Closed','Complete','Close','Issued Without Contractor') AND Permit_Type <> 'Design Review'
rate_limit: ArcGIS hosted FeatureServer query, 1,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily.

scope.status_set: Issued-proven statuses only: Issued, Finaled, Expired, Closed, Complete, Close, 'Issued Without Contractor' (70,199 of 75,570 rows filed in the window at File_Date >= 2025-10-17). Every other status is a pre-issuance or never-issued state and is not pulled: Pending, Plan Review, In Review, Awaiting Client Reply, Incomplete Submittal, Accepted, Approved, Partial Approval, Approved w/Conditions, Administrative Approval, Pending Fees, Pending HCLC Review, Hold, Continued, Appeal, Opt-Out (review pipeline, not yet issued — 'Approved' alone is plan approval; 8,303 records all-time sit there, newest filed 2026-10-14, so the distinction is live practice, not a legacy artifact), and Void, Withdrawn, Denied, Closed By Rule (never issued). Excluded rows are not 'held' records — they are out of the published population by definition, exactly like San Francisco's non-primary address rows.
scope.type_exclusion: Permit_Type 'Design Review' is excluded at pull time (pull_where_extra): a design-review approval authorizes no construction (the San Antonio non-construction rule). Measured exact: 193 rows / 185 permits in the issued window; a permit's rows never mix types (0 groups disagree on Permit_Type), so the exclusion removes whole permits only. 'Urban Forestry' needed no filter: 0 of its records stand in an issued-proven status in the window.

update_cadence: Hourly during business hours per the item description; MEASURED 2026-10-18: layer dataLastEditDate 2026-10-16T21:25:29Z and newest File_Date 2026-10-16 (Friday) on a Sunday audit — consistent with business-hours updates and a weekend pause. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the layer's editingInfo.dataLastEditDate; the 96h threshold absorbs the weekend pause.
watermark_field: File_Date + Permit_No — refresh re-pulls the full trailing-12-month window nightly and upserts: the feed's records change status IN PLACE (an application filed in the window enters the published set when it reaches an issued-proven status), so a watermark-only pull would miss status transitions; the full-window re-pull is this registry's refresh shape (gate 4's count baseline is computed on the identical where).
